practice: Antimicrobial treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria in diabetic women
old_belief: US groups recommended screening for and treating asymptomatic bacteriuria in women with diabetes.
new_finding: Randomized trial found this practice leads to more antibiotic use without reducing complications or improving time to symptomatic infection.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2

practice: High-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell transplantation added to conventional adjuvant chemotherapy for high-risk breast cancer
old_belief: Believed to improve disease-free survival by 20-30% beyond standard adjuvant chemotherapy; became common, costly, and controversial practice for over a decade.
new_finding: Randomized trial found reduced risk of relapse but no improvement in overall survival.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2

practice: Allergen-impermeable bed covers for adults with asthma
old_belief: US and European guidelines recommended allergen-impermeable bed covers for asthma/allergic rhinitis patients; industry cost in the billions.
new_finding: Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial (>1100 patients) found no benefit on any clinical or physiologic outcome.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2

practice: Methylprednisolone and/or valacyclovir for vestibular neuritis
old_belief: Physicians prescribed either or both corticosteroid and antiviral, with unclear evidence for either.
new_finding: Randomized 2x2 factorial trial found only corticosteroids (not antiviral) improved recovery.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2

practice: Mild intraoperative hypothermia during intracranial aneurysm surgery
old_belief: Used in nearly 50% of aneurysm surgeries as a presumed neuroprotective adjunct since 1955.
new_finding: Large randomized trial (IHAST) found no improvement in neurologic outcomes, with an increase in bacterial infections.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2

practice: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) added to optimal medical therapy for stable coronary artery disease
old_belief: PCI was a common initial treatment strategy alongside intensive medical therapy for stable coronary artery disease.
new_finding: Trial (COURAGE) found PCI added to optimal medical therapy did not reduce risk of death, MI, or other major cardiovascular events.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2
note: Directly relevant precedent for RGU scenario and DGP method design -- a well-known temporal-directionality reversal in cardiology.

practice: In vitro fertilization (IVF) with preimplantation genetic screening for advanced maternal age
old_belief: Preimplantation genetic screening had become increasingly common to improve IVF outcomes in women of advanced maternal age.
new_finding: Multicenter double-blind RCT found screening significantly REDUCED rates of ongoing pregnancies and live births.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2

practice: Intensive glucose lowering (target HbA1c <7.0%) in type 2 diabetes
old_belief: Target hemoglobin A1c of 7.0% or less was recommended for most patients with diabetes.
new_finding: ACCORD trial found this intensive target sustained for 3.5 years increased mortality without significantly reducing major cardiovascular events, vs. a more permissive goal.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2
note: Overlaps existing pilot concept 'tight glycemic control ICU harm' (C0017725) in data/clmi_prescreen_v2 -- can directly upgrade to Gold-tier using this citation.

old_belief: Revascularization was performed in 16% of patients with newly diagnosed atherosclerotic renovascular disease and hypertension, presumed beneficial.
new_finding: Large RCT (ASTRAL) of revascularization plus medical management vs. medical management alone found substantial risks but no evidence of benefit from revascularization.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2

practice: Gentamicin-collagen sponge for infection prophylaxis in colorectal surgery
old_belief: Approved and used in millions of patients worldwide since 1985; a single-center RCT found a 70% decrease in surgical site infection.
new_finding: Large multicenter phase 3 trial found the sponge paradoxically resulted in significantly MORE surgical site infections and more subsequent hospitalizations.
source: Prasad et al. 2013, Mayo Clinic Proceedings 88(8):790-798, Table 2
